| WS22 | **A subtask draft is a treeitem, and Undo carries the title it started with.** The open "add a subtask" field sat in the list as a `fieldset`, which `role="tree"` does not own — axe fails it as a critical `aria-required-children` violation, and a group would have to own treeitems of its own. It is now a `treeitem` one level under its parent, last in that parent's children, with `aria-setsize="-1"` because it is not in the set until it is saved, and `tabIndex={-1}` because the field inside it takes focus. Separately, the Undo of a move looked the task's title up again when it ran — by which time the task is in the collection it was moved to, which the browser may never have loaded — so the toast read "Moved “this task” back to Now". `move` takes the title the first toast used. | Build default | Architecture §10.4, decisions P3, WS17 |
| WS23 | **The rail's drop destinations are addressed through an exported selector.** The workspace's drag layer marks a collection's rail item as a drop target by finding it in the shell's own DOM. It did so with a class name written out at the call site, so renaming the markup would have disabled every rail drop target silently — no error, no failing test. `components/shell/workspace.tsx` exports `railItemSelector(collection)`, `app-shell.test.tsx` requires the rail to keep matching it, and the drop label re-measures its anchor while it is shown instead of keeping a rect taken once at render. The label is `aria-hidden`: the drag layer's `Accessibility` plugin already announces the same destination on `dragover`, and a live region would have read it twice. | Build default | Architecture §2.3, §10.4, decision W9 |
| WS24 | **The task tree always has a tab stop.** The list, not the row, decides which `treeitem` carries `tabindex="0"`: the focused row while it is on screen, otherwise the first row shown. `activeRow` starts as null and a search or a collapsed parent can take the focused row off screen, and in both states every row carried `tabindex="-1"`, so Tab skipped the whole tree and the list was reachable only with a pointer. `keyboard.test.tsx` fails if no row is tabbable before anything has been focused, and if the tab stop does not come back to the first row when the focused one is hidden. | Build default | WAI-ARIA tree pattern; architecture §10.2; W9 |
| WS25 | **The parent-with-subtasks question falls back to the task's own detail.** `TaskCommands.complete` counted open subtasks from the loaded list alone, so completing from the task page header with no list loaded behind it (a direct link, a list still loading) archived the subtasks without asking, against decision P1. It now falls back to the detail's `childCount`, and names a count only when it knows the whole subtree. | Build default | P1; WS6 |
| WS26 | **The web client keeps a bounded number of task details.** `TaskStore` held a detail entry for every task opened in a session and refetched all of them on a reconnect or an unnamed `tasks.changed`, a request per task the person had moved on from (§3). It keeps the 20 most recently loaded, never one mid-request, and `useTaskDetail` loads a dropped one again when its pane still shows it. The api's ownership read for a worker `task_tree.changed` hint is likewise split across a batch, because 100 hinted ids and the owner are one parameter more than a statement may bind. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §3.2; WS3 |
| WS27 | **An archive record stays named once it is known.** The archive detail read its record out of the current listing page only, so a record opened from its address past the first page, and a record just restored out of the listing, both answered "This task isn't available". It keeps the record it has (keyed by task id) and reads the task itself when the listing does not hold it. | Build default | Archive brief; WS9; P2 |
## Search (Phase D1)

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | **Index layout and tokenizer.** One MiniSearch 7.2.0 index per account over the fields `title`, `heading`, `body` and the opt-in `chat`; section bodies longer than 1,200 characters are indexed as chunks overlapping by 80 characters at whitespace. The plaintext artifact is JSON holding the MiniSearch plain object plus task records, section chunks and messages (snippets and grouping come from them), sealed as a `SYMO` object envelope with kind `search_index`, object id `<generation>-<writeId>` and format version `INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION` 1, at `u/<ownerId>/search/<generation>-<writeId>.idx`. Normalization: NFKD, strip `\p{M}`, lowercase, NFKD and strip again, fold table 1 (`ß`→`ss`, `æ`→`ae`, `œ`→`oe`, `ø`→`o`, `đ`/`ð`→`d`, `ł`→`l`, `ı`→`i`, `þ`→`th`, `ħ`→`h`, `ŧ`→`t`), apostrophes removed, terms cut at 64 UTF-16 units; words come from `Intl.Segmenter("en", { granularity: "word" })` with a fixed locale. The tokenizer fingerprint names these rules, never the ICU build, so an api and a worker on different Node patch releases never rebuild each other's indexes. Limits: 16 million indexed characters per account, 1 MiB of text and 2,000 sections per document, 8,000 characters per message, 4,096 per title; content cut at a limit makes results `partial` with notice `index_truncated`. | Build default | Architecture §10.1; research core-libs §5 (`ß` folding left open) |
| S2 | **Ranking, matching and snippets.** Match kinds rank `title_exact`, `title_prefix` (title terms start with the query, the last term as a prefix), `title_terms`, `title_typo`, `heading` (every term in the heading), `body`, `chat`. Typos apply to titles only: none under 5 code points (so `book` never matches `look`), one edit from 5 to 8, two from 9. Prefixes match from one character in titles and two in text. Terms combine with AND; a multiword query without quoted phrases falls back to results matching some terms (notice `partial_terms`, ranked by terms matched) only when nothing matches every term. Double-quoted phrases must appear contiguously; unquoted multiword queries rank contiguous occurrences first. Within a kind, scores within 25% of each other are similar and the most recently updated task wins, then the id. Hits group per task; a group shows its three best sections and messages with counts, fifty when `taskId` expands it. Snippets are a 180-character window starting at a word boundary about a third before the first phrase or term match, whitespace collapsed, with at most 16 UTF-16 highlight ranges; nothing produces markup. Measured on 2,000 sections (2.4 million characters, 5.7 MB artifact, Apple M4, Node 24.15): build 404 ms, seal 147 ms, open 70 ms, 15 ms per query with snippets. | Build default | Note 14 |
| S3 | **`search_indexes` and the intent lifecycle.** The first publication creates the row at generation 1; beyond §10.1's columns it keeps `include_chat`, `truncated`, `byte_size`, `executor_generation`, `created_at` and `updated_at`. The writer reads executor state, the row, a bounded batch of unapplied intents, their summary, the account key and `deletion_state` in one batch, publishes with `If-None-Match: *`, then advances the row with a generation compare-and-set guarded by the executor mode and generation and `deletion_state = 'none'`, deleting intents up to `applied_through` in the same batch (guarded by its write id), so `search_intents` holds only unapplied changes. The loser of a race deletes its object; an unknown outcome is reconciled by reading the write id back; each publication deletes up to 20 older objects of generations at or below it. A rebuild from D1 and current heads runs when the row is missing, format or fingerprint differ, the object is missing, undecryptable or inconsistent, or the chat opt-in differs from `include_chat`; its `applied_through` is the highest intent read before any record. | Build default | Architecture §3.2, §10.1 |
| S4 | **Query service.** The index row, pending summary and wrapped account key are cached 5 seconds per owner (invalidated by publications). Decrypted indexes live in a 128 MB least-recently-used cache counted in plaintext bytes, dropped after 10 idle minutes, keyed by the requester's `access_generation` (an entry loaded under another generation is evicted), and evicted by the `search_cache_eviction` restriction effect. Unpublished intents (at most 200, re-reading at most 10 documents and 200 messages) form an in-memory overlay that shadows the published index; beyond the bound results are `partial`. With no readable index, up to 5,000 titles read from D1 are searched with status `rebuilding`, an unreadable generation is not downloaded again for 60 seconds, and the writer is asked to rebuild; intents waiting over 2 minutes ask for the writer again. Cursors are base64url JSON `[1, generation, pendingThrough, offset, digest]` over the normalized query and effective scope; a cursor is served from the view it was ranked over while that generation is held (two views per owner) and otherwise answers 409 `search.cursor_stale` with `details.indexGeneration`. Every page re-reads its tasks, their parents and head revisions from D1 in one batch and drops tasks that are gone or out of scope, reporting `titleStale` and per-section `stale` against the current head. A failing source answers 503 `search.unavailable`. | Build default | Architecture §3.3, §10.1 |
| S5 | **Search sources are per-domain contributors.** Search reads titles from `tasks` itself, decrypting with purpose `title`, table `tasks`, row id = task id, column `title_enc`, which the workspace feature must also write with. Documents (`DocumentTextSource`: plain-text sections of current heads plus a head-revision statement), messages (`MessageTextSource`, task conversations only), the chat opt-in (`ChatOptInSource`) and deadline filters (`DeadlineFilterSource`) come from `core/src/search/sources/contributors/<domain>.ts`, which the documents, Simon, preferences and scheduling features fill, as with the events and purge contributors. Until they do, only titles are indexed, chat stays excluded (the §10.1 opt-in default) and deadline filters answer 422 `search.filter_unavailable`; in-memory implementations serve tests. Producers record intents with `searchIntentStatement` guarded by their deciding write and, in durable mode, call `enqueueSearchIndex`. The search archive contributor records a task intent per archived task in the complete batch. | Build default | Architecture §2.3, §10.1 |
| S6 | **Writer scheduling.** With `DURABLE=false` the api coordinator runs the writer in process, one owner at a time: 30 seconds after a change request, at once for a rebuild, up to 10 batches per run, backing off failures from 30 seconds to 10 minutes; while the local scheduler is active it also sweeps every 30 seconds for owners whose intents waited 30 seconds. With `DURABLE=true` the api only enqueues `search-index` (once per owner per 30-second window); the task (`d1` queue, `micro`, three attempts, `small-1x` after OOM, `maxDuration` 300) publishes up to 20 batches within 4 minutes, announces `search.index_published {generation, pending}` (the api re-reads D1 and relays `search.freshness`), and enqueues the next window with a `scope: "global"` key when changes remain. Re-enqueueing owners whose intents waited 5 minutes in durable mode belongs to `cleanup-hourly`, which calls `staleSearchOwners` and `enqueueSearchIndex`. | Build default | Architecture §8.8, §10.1 |
| S7 | **Search API and index lifecycle.** `GET /v1/search`, `GET /v1/search/titles` and `GET /v1/search/freshness` are `app`-class, admitted-only reads without idempotency; filters are comma lists (`collections`, `types`), `archive=exclude\|include\|only`, `taskId`, and the typed deadline filter (`deadline`, `deadlineFrom`, `deadlineTo`, `timeZone`); page size 1 to 50 (default 20), title results 1 to 20 (default 8). Every response reports `status`, `indexGeneration` and `pendingIntents` beside the results, and full search adds `scope` and `notices`. Key rotation: each index object's own key is wrapped by the account data key, so `CONTENT_KEK` rotation keeps indexes readable (decision CR1); backups: R2 is unversioned and the index is derived, so a lost or corrupt object is rebuilt; purge: the R2 step deletes `u/<userId>/search/` and the search purge contributor deletes intents and the row in bounded batches; the crypto-shred makes every index unreadable at once. | Build default | Note 14; architecture §5.6, §10.1 |
| S8 | **Feature restriction effects (platform fix).** `RestrictionEffectRegistry` in `apps/api/src/common/access/access.providers.ts`, exported by `PlatformModule`, lets feature modules register post-commit restriction effects from `onModuleInit`. `RestrictionEffects` runs them after the access cache eviction and before sockets close, isolating and logging each failure; account deletion runs them too. The platform's effect list was fixed at construction with no seam for §5.5's "evicts access, grant and search caches"; search registers `search_cache_eviction`, and grant caches can use the same seam. | Build default | Architecture §5.5; decisions C6.4, CZ.5 |
| S9 | **Foundation schema tests allow feature migrations (platform fix).** `schema.test.ts` now requires every foundation table among the migrated tables (all tables still STRICT) instead of exactly the foundation list, and `migrations.test.ts` requires files below `0100` to stay in `0001`–`0019` and every file within `0001`–`1099`, because feature ranges share the migrations directory (§3.4) and any feature migration failed the old tests. | Build default | Architecture §3.4 |
| S10 | **A search query never leaves page memory.** The full search screen keeps its query, filters and the place it came from in a module-level store, not in the address bar, `sessionStorage` or `localStorage`, so returning from a task restores the search while no raw query enters browser history or a server log (note 14: "do not persist sensitive raw query history by default", "avoid raw query/snippet logging"). The palette seeds that store before invoking `search.full_search`, and a reload or sign-out (a full document navigation) forgets it. A task opened from a result carries only opaque ids in its address (`?section=<sectionId>`, `?message=<messageId>`, `SEARCH_JUMP_PARAMS`); the heading, revision, staleness and query travel in the in-memory jump that `consumeSearchJump(taskId)` hands to the documents and Simon panes once. | Build default | Note 14; architecture §6.3 |
| S11 | **Palette behavior.** One overlay (`features/search/command-palette.tsx`) renders the quick switcher and the shortcut help from one store, mounted once in the shell's palette slot. Tasks mode debounces 140 ms and asks `GET /v1/search/titles` (8 results); an empty query lists up to 5 recent tasks by reading `GET /v1/preferences/recent` and then each task, dropping archived and removed ones; `>` at the start, the Actions toggle, or Backspace on an empty actions query switches modes; "Search all content" always sits last. It is a combobox with `aria-activedescendant` over a listbox, so Up, Down, Enter and Escape work with focus in the field; a disabled action shows its reason and never runs; the choice runs after the overlay closes, so focus lands where the action puts it, and opening a task focuses the page region. Escape returns focus where it came from, or to the profile menu's trigger when the menu opened the overlay. A signed-out or unadmitted session never queries. | Build default | command_palette.md; note 13; §10.2 |
| S12 | **Full search screen.** `/search` is a client screen with the query focused on arrival, visible collection, archive, content-type and deadline filters (at least one collection and one content type stay selected), and the effective scope, taken from the response, stated in one sentence above the results. Results group per task with heading, snippet, archived and stale labels; `taskId` expands one task's matches in place; `nextCursor` pages with "Show more results" and a stale cursor restarts the list. A malformed date range is refused in the client and `search.filter_unavailable` offers "Clear deadline filter". Freshness is polled every 15 seconds only while the shown page is behind (`status` not `ready` or pending changes) and `search.freshness` events feed the same store; a newer generation offers a refresh instead of replacing what is on screen. Opening a result re-reads the task first, so a moved task opens in its current collection and a removed one is dropped with a notice instead of a wrong jump. | Build default | search.md; note 14; §10.1 |
| S13 | **Find within a surface is a seam.** `/` focuses the field the visible surface marks with `data-surface-find` (`SURFACE_FIND_ATTRIBUTE`), preferring the focused pane, and reports "This view has nothing to search" when there is none, so documents and Simon add their find fields without search knowing about them. `InboxFind` (`features/search/inbox-find.tsx`) is the task list's field: it filters that collection alone through `GET /v1/search?collections=<c>&types=tasks&archive=exclude`, shows the collection's own list whenever it is empty, and offers "Search all content" so touch users reach the full screen without a keyboard. The workspace feature mounts it around its task tree. | Build default | Note 14 (entry point 3); note 13 |
| S14 | **Three platform seams for the keyboard surfaces (platform fixes).** (1) `ActionsContextValue.availability(actionId, source, pane?)` (over `KeyboardDispatcher.check`) reports whether an action could run, without running it: the palette and the shortcut help must show disabled actions and their reasons, and the provider exposed no way to ask. (2) The profile menu's "Keyboard shortcuts" entry now invokes `SHORTCUT_HELP_ACTION_ID` (declared beside `SIGN_OUT_ACTION_ID` in `actions/shell-actions.ts`) so `?` and the menu open the same overlay; Settings keeps the remapping UI, which the overlay links to. (3) `components/shell/workspace.tsx` crashed the whole app ("Panel constraints not found for Panel sym-chat-panel") whenever a task opened through client-side navigation: the collapse sync called the panel's imperative API in the commit that mounted it. The sync is now retried on the next frame, which matters for every feature that opens a task from a list, the palette or a result. | Build default | §10.2; decision W8, W9 |
| S15 | **`search_used` is reported through a seam.** Search builds the allowlisted properties (surface, the two opt-in booleans and a bucketed count, never a query or a title) and hands them to a reporter the analytics feature registers with `setSearchUsedReporter`; without one nothing is sent and nothing is queued, so search never loads a provider or touches consent. | Build default | Decision C5.3; architecture §15 |
| S16 | **The search e2e spec serves the api from contract-shaped fixtures.** `apps/e2e/tests/search.spec.ts` intercepts `/v1/*` and answers with exactly the shapes `@symplist/contracts` defines, because signing in (access) and creating tasks (workspace) belong to other features and are not built yet; the browser client validates every response against those schemas, so a drifting contract still fails the spec. It covers the palette's keyboard-only sequence, full search with the archive opt-in and opening a result, the empty, no-match, failure and rebuilding states, the phone surface, dark mode and the help overlay with focus restored, at 1440, 1024 and 390 px with axe checks and evidence under `apps/e2e/evidence/search/`. An api-backed run belongs with the integrator once access and workspace land. | Build default | Architecture §17; §2.3 |
| S17 | **Both shortcut surfaces stay in the profile menu (refines S14).** S14 replaced the menu's "Keyboard shortcuts" link with the overlay-opening item, which left Settings → Keyboard shortcuts — the remapping surface the workspace feature builds at `/settings/shortcuts` — reachable only from inside the overlay, and deleted a `menuLinks` row the other three feature branches keep. The link is restored unchanged, so `menuLinks` merges cleanly, and the overlay entry sits beside it as "Shortcut help" (the `search.show_shortcuts` label, matching the action in the palette) so the two surfaces never read as one. `app-shell.test.tsx` asserts both entries. | Build default | keyboard_shortcuts.md; §10.2; decision S14 |
| S18 | **Source files stay textual for the four-branch merge.** `use-async-search.ts` carried a literal NUL character inside the request-key template, which made git classify the file as binary — no diff, no three-way merge. It is written as the `\0` escape instead; the runtime separator is byte-identical. | Build default | Architecture §17 |
| S19 | **Search results are decrypted by the api, not the browser.** §10.1 puts the per-user MiniSearch index in R2 encrypted under a per-object key wrapped by the account data key (§4, decision S7/CR1) and has the api load, decrypt and query it behind `GET /v1/search` — its LRU is "bounded by total decrypted bytes". The browser holds no account key, so the web stage validates already-plaintext responses against the contracts and adds no client-side decryption; end-to-end encryption is the Vault's property (§11), and "Vault never enters the index". | Build default | Architecture §4, §10.1, §11; decision S7 |
| S20 | **Index freshness is polled only for what a publication can change.** `useFreshnessWatch` polled `GET /v1/search/freshness` every 15 s whenever the response status was not `ready`, but §10.1 `partial` also covers conditions no publication ever clears: an account past the index size limit (`search_indexes.truncated`) makes every search partial forever, and a broad query is partial through `results_capped`. Each open search surface therefore polled for as long as it stayed on screen, one D1 request per poll against the 2 req/s api lane (§3.1), learning nothing. The poll now runs while the index is rebuilding, while intents are pending, or while the chat rebuild named by the `chat_indexing` notice is still coming — the only `partial` a later generation resolves. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §10.1; note 14 |
| S21 | **Test harnesses stay out of published builds.** `packages/core/tsconfig.json` excluded only `*.test.ts`, so `src/search/harness.test-support.ts` — which creates temp directories, a local SQLite database and a generated key provider — compiled into `packages/core/dist` and shipped to the api and worker images. The exclude now lists `src/**/*.test-support.ts`, matching `packages/search/tsconfig.json`; `tsconfig.typecheck.json` still includes all of `src`, so the harness keeps its type coverage. | Build default | Architecture §2.2, §17 |
## Access feature (Phase D1, backend)

Decisions made while building sign-in, beta access, administration and account deletion requests against [architecture](architecture.md) §5, notes 03 and 04 and the access screen briefs.

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 | **Access routes and error codes.** Pre-session: `POST /v1/auth/lookup` (200 `{exists}`), `/signup` (201, body `{email, consent: true}`), `/otp` (201) and `/otp/verify` (200, the `GET /v1/me` body). App class: `POST /v1/auth/logout`, `GET /v1/me` (identity), `PUT /v1/me/name` and `POST /v1/me/onboarding/complete` (admitted), `POST /v1/access/redeem` (identity, Idempotency-Key), `POST /v1/account/deletion/otp`, `/verify` and `POST /v1/account/deletion` (identity, fresh, 202), and the admin routes under `/v1/admin/invites`, `/accounts`, `/campaigns/:id/revocation/{preview,confirm}` and `/activity` (admin, fresh). `GET /v1/me` adds `destination` (`app`, `onboarding`, `beta_gate`, `paused`) and `betaAccessRequired`, so every client routes the same way. The access error codes are `auth.account_not_found` 404, `auth.account_exists` and `auth.account_unavailable` 409, `auth.delivery_failed` 502, `otp.incorrect` 400 (`details.attemptsRemaining`), `otp.expired` and `otp.attempts_exhausted` 410, `otp.locked`, `otp.cooldown` and `otp.send_limited` 429 (`details.retryAfter`), `invite.invalid` 422, `invite.changed` and `invite.revoked` 409, `invite.capacity_below_used` and `invite.expiry_invalid` 422, `admin.state_changed`, `admin.action_unavailable` and `admin.preview_stale` 409, `onboarding.name_required` 409 and `account.deletion_unauthorized` 403. | Build default | Architecture §5.1, §5.4, §6 |
| AC2 | **Lookup and signup semantics.** Lookup reports `exists: true` for verified accounts and accounts being deleted; a pending registration that never verified reports `false`, so the person confirms signup again, which reuses the pending account (idempotent) and sends a new signup code. A signup for a verified address answers `auth.account_exists` and sends nothing; the client offers a sign-in code. Lookup and signup are also limited in memory per address (10 per 10 minutes, keyed by the address's `otp-limit-email` digest, never the address) besides the per-IP bucket. | Build default | Note 03 (lookup reveals existence), §5.1 ("throttled by IP and email") |
| AC3 | **OTP mechanics.** Verification reads the challenge, then one batch reserves an attempt only while the challenge is live, has attempts left and the address is not locked out, and applies either the consumption with the caller's guarded effects (session, deletion authorization) or the failure count; a result never counts without a reserved attempt, so concurrent guesses cannot exceed the per-challenge budget and a refused reservation never reveals whether the code was right. Counts live on the address's existing `otp_limits` row under any configured digest version (a row under the current version starts only when none exists), so rotating `OTP_DIGEST_SECRET` never resets them. Each failure beyond the daily limit while the window lasts locks for another hour. The resend cooldown ignores consumed challenges. A challenge whose email could not be handed to the provider is deleted (its hourly and daily counts stay), and one retryable provider failure is retried at once with the same idempotency key. Session-bound purposes (`account_delete`, `vault_reset`) are sent with `OtpService.sendForSession` and verified with a user and session binding. Core defines an `OtpMailer` port implemented in the api over the email package, because `@symplist/core` has no JSX typecheck. | Build default | Architecture §5.1, §5.8 |
| AC4 | **Redemption details.** The §5.4 statement matches `i.digest IN (<digest under every configured version>)`. `request_id` is `redeem:<userId>:<Idempotency-Key>`, so a retry after an unknown outcome finds its own seat. A relocked or suspended account is refused with `access.relocked` before an unlocked beta state returns `already_unlocked`, so a suspended account never gets a success. With `BETA_ACCESS_REQUIRED=false` no seat is claimed. The follow-up applies only while the account is still locked at the seat's epoch, not suspended, not being deleted and without a current grant; a seat whose account was relocked in between stays consumed and never unlocks. A claimed seat without a grant is finalized by the next redemption request of the account (instead of `invite.invalid`), by `GET /v1/me`, and by the reconciler: an hourly local-scheduler job at :20 when `DURABLE=false`, and a 15-minute api timer when `DURABLE=true` (where the local scheduler never runs). | Build default | Architecture §5.4 |
| AC5 | **Beta tables beyond the §5.4 constraints.** `beta_invites` adds `campaign_id` (one per generation request), `mode`, `label_enc` with `label_owner_id` (the creating administrator's key), `revoked_by`, `version` (for `expectedVersion`) and `write_id`; there is no redemption count column. `beta_redemptions` keeps exactly the §5.4 columns and constraints, has no foreign key to `users` and is never purged, because seats are never refunded and `COUNT(*) + 1` seat numbers must stay contiguous. `beta_access_grants` has `source` (`invite`, `admin`), `source_id` (the redemption id, or the admin event id), `campaign_id`, `access_epoch`, actor, encrypted reason and `revoked_reason`, `UNIQUE (source, source_id)`, one current grant per account (partial unique index) and a foreign key to `users`; the access purge contributor deletes an account's grants and clears labels written under its shredded key. | Build default | Architecture §3.4, §5.4, §5.6; note 04 records |
| AC6 | **Invite generation.** One folded `@OneTimeSecret(["codes"])` batch inserts every invite of the request with one `json_each` statement, appends one `invite_generated` event and records the redacted outcome. `codes` is an array of `SYM-` strings aligned with `invites`, because the one-time-secret redactor treats every string inside a secret field as secret and would refuse invite ids there. Codes are 20 random bytes in RFC 4648 Base32; normalization (NFKC, upper case, whitespace and separators removed, optional `SYM` prefix) is shared by web and api in `@symplist/contracts`; the hint is the last four characters. A batch holds at most 100 codes, a bound email applies to a single code, and the expiry must be more than a minute and at most 365 days away. Inventory search matches the hint (as typed, as displayed or from a pasted code), the bound email, or the decrypted label, scanning at most 2,000 invites per request and returning a scan cursor when that budget ends first. | Build default | Note 04 (generation, show once), architecture §6.1 |
| AC7 | **Invite edits and audit.** Each edit (capacity, expiry, revoke) is one batch whose audit event is inserted only while the invite is at `expectedVersion`, not revoked and the edit is valid, and whose update applies only when that event exists, so the event carries the before values read in the same transaction and a retried request applies nothing twice. A cap may go down to the seats already used; an expiry must be later than the current one (an expired invite becomes active again). Audit events expose the campaign and its decrypted label for "Maya redeemed Friends — September". | Build default | Admin invites and activity briefs |
| AC8 | **Account actions.** Unlock, relock, restore eligibility and restore access each need a reason (at most 500 characters, encrypted under the target account's key, provisioning the key for a pending account) and the `accessGeneration` the administrator saw. Unlock applies to any locked account, including one that never verified, and never verifies the email. Unlock and restore access revoke any grant a campaign revocation left current before inserting the new admin grant. Relock runs `restrictStatements` with its audit event guarded by the restriction write id and then `afterRestriction`; its generation check is a fresh read just before, because the restriction's deciding statement takes no extra condition. After every action the account's sessions are evicted, identity-level sockets re-read and `access.changed` published. | Build default | Architecture §5.4, §5.5 |
| AC9 | **Campaign revocation.** The membership is every account with a current grant from the campaign that is not being deleted; `previewDigest` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the campaign id and the sorted `(userId, grantId)` pairs. The confirmation recomputes it, then restricts at most five accounts per batch, each with a `campaign_access_revoked` event (request id `<request>:<userId>`), runs the post-commit effects per batch and publishes `access.changed` per account. | Build default | Architecture §5.5 |
| AC10 | **Admin bootstrap.** Besides setting `role = 'admin'`, the one conditional batch admits a `locked` account (`beta_state = 'unlocked'`, `access_generation + 1`), because the `admin` level requires an admitted account; it never touches `relocked` or suspended accounts. The admin grant is inserted only when the account has no current grant. Forced re-bootstrap records an `admin_rebootstrap` event with the operator's actor id and encrypted reason and applies only to an account that is not already an administrator. The CLI is `apps/api/src/modules/access/admin-bootstrap.cli.ts` (`node --env-file-if-exists=.env dist/modules/access/admin-bootstrap.cli.js`), exiting 0 when it promoted, 1 when nothing changed or it failed, and 2 for usage or configuration errors; the `admin:bootstrap` package script is left to the integrator (no manifest edits in feature branches). | Build default | Architecture §5.7, decision R13 |
| AC11 | **Onboarding and identity.** `PUT /v1/me/name` stores the NFC-normalized, whitespace-collapsed name (1 to 80 characters, no control or format characters) encrypted under the account key and moves onboarding from `name` to `connections`; it is admitted-only, so locked accounts only view identity, sign out and delete. `POST /v1/me/onboarding/complete` finishes onboarding from `connections` (Continue or Skip for now), is a no-op when already done and answers `onboarding.name_required` before the name step. Onboarding changes publish `access.changed`, since the step is part of the access state. PUT is a full replacement and needs no Idempotency-Key. | Build default | Onboarding and settings account briefs |
| AC12 | **Test-only OTP outbox.** With `NODE_ENV=test` the api keeps the latest delivered code per address and purpose in memory and serves it from `POST /v1/auth/test/otp` (`pre_session` class) for the end-to-end suite. In any other environment the outbox is not constructed and the route answers `not_found` before reading its body. | Build default | Architecture §17 (e2e over a local api) |
| AC13 | **Platform tests adjusted for feature migrations and routes.** The foundation schema test now requires the foundation tables to exist (feature ranges add more), the migration range test accepts `0100`–`1099`, the restriction registry test no longer expects every contributor to be empty, and the limits probe routes moved to `/v1/auth/probe-lookup` and `/v1/auth/probe-signup` because the real lookup and signup routes shadowed them. Access api test helpers live in `apps/api/test/access/`, and the contributor tests live beside the domain folders rather than inside the contributor folders, whose registry test counts every file. | Build default | Decisions C3-3, C6.4, C6.7 |

## Access feature (Phase D1, web)

Decisions made while building the access screens, the session runtime and beta administration in `apps/web` against [architecture](architecture.md) §5, §6, §13, §15 and the access screen briefs. They extend the backend rulings AC1-AC13 and never change them.

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC14 | **One session per document.** The access feature implements the §2.3 session seam with a single `SessionStore` per document: one `GET /v1/me` shared by every gate, replaced in place by the bodies of the calls that change the caller's own access (verify, redeem, name, onboarding complete), refreshed by the realtime `access.changed` event and by a tab becoming visible after 60 seconds, and never read on the server. `SessionGate require="identity" \| "admitted" \| "admin"` renders children only while the level holds, so a locked, paused or signed-out person never sees protected content behind an overlay; the api stays the only authority. A `loading` phase with a load error shows a retry rather than guessing a state. | Build default | Architecture §5.1, §5.4, §7; beta_gate.md, access_revoked.md |
| AC15 | **Route groups by access level.** `(auth)` holds `/signin`, `/signin/verify` and `/signin/create` (no session); `(gate)` holds `/access`, `/access/paused` and `/access/account` at `identity`; `(onboarding)` holds `/welcome` and `/welcome/connections` at `identity`; `(app)` is `admitted`, and `/admin/*` adds `admin`. Moving between the app and an analytics-excluded group is a document navigation (`navigateAcrossGroups`), so no protected state or analytics client survives the move (§15). The administratively revoked and suspended states share one `/access/paused` screen with no redeem form, because another invite must not lift a restriction. | Build default | Architecture §5.4, §15; access_revoked.md |
| AC16 | **Optimistic proxy redirect on a session hint.** `apps/web/src/proxy.ts` redirects a visitor with no `sym_hint` cookie to `/signin?next=<path>`, with `/signin` the only public prefix. The cookie is the api's non-secret presence marker: the proxy never reads a session, never calls the api, and every screen behind it checks `GET /v1/me` again, which is what actually decides what renders. The redirect keeps the request's Content Security Policy header. | Build default | Architecture §5.1, §10.4 |
| AC17 | **Sign-out is one path.** The profile menu, the gate screens, Settings → Account and the `access.sign_out` command all call `signOutOfBrowser()`: `POST /v1/auth/logout`, then registered feature cleanups, the appearance cookie, the analytics identity, the cached CSRF token and every `symplist.access.*` storage key, then `/signin` as a new document. A session the api had already ended counts as signed out; any other failure keeps the person signed in and shows a retry, so nothing claims a sign-out that did not happen. Account deletion accepted by the api marks the same exit so no gate starts a competing redirect. | Build default | profile_menu.md, settings_account.md, architecture §5.1, §15 |
| AC18 | **The Settings shell is a route layout.** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/layout.tsx` renders `SettingsFrame` (the section list, the phone selector and Back to workspace), so every section — Account, Appearance, Notifications, Keyboard shortcuts, Connections, Agent connections, About — shares one shell and each page renders only its own content. Sections owned by other features need no shell of their own. There is no Billing section. | Build default | settings_account.md |
| AC19 | **Seams for features outside this wave.** The connections onboarding step takes an optional `catalogue` node from the connections feature (§14) and, without it, says plainly that this deployment has no connectors yet instead of showing broken tiles; Settings → Account leaves `data-slot="account-privacy"` for the analytics feature's Privacy section (§15, decision D5). Both are the seam, not a stub to replace. | Build default | onboarding_connections.md, settings_account.md, §15 |
| AC20 | **CSRF classes at the call site.** The browser client sends `X-Symplist-CSRF: 1` for the four `pre_session` routes (lookup, signup, OTP send, OTP verify) and the session-bound token from `GET /v1/auth/csrf` for every other unsafe `/v1/*` call, dropping the cached token on a 403 so the next call fetches a fresh one. Idempotency-Key is sent exactly for the routes the api marks `@Idempotent` (redeem, invite generation and edits, account actions, campaign revocation confirm, account deletion) and never for a preview or a full-replacement PUT. | Build default | Architecture §5.3, §6.1; decision AC1 |
| AC21 | **One api and one administrator per end-to-end run.** `apps/e2e/tests/access.spec.ts` starts the api once behind a directory lock, under a supervisor that stops it when the Playwright runner exits, and signs the bootstrap operator in once into a saved storage state, because one address may only be sent a few codes an hour (§5.1) and every project needs an administrator. Codes come from the test-only outbox (AC12). | Build default | Architecture §17, decision AC12 |
| AC22 | **A step never leaves before its own state arrives.** `SignInFlowProvider` reads the sign-in flow from session storage in an effect, and a child's effect runs before its provider's, so every step (`/signin/create`, `/signin/verify`) waits for the flow's `hydrated` flag before deciding there is nothing to continue. Without it a reload on the code step redirected to the email entry and discarded a live challenge. Any future consumer of `useSignInFlow()` must read `hydrated` before treating an empty flow as empty. | Review fix | Architecture §5.1; email_otp.md, signup_confirmation.md |
## Documents and Git (Phase D1)

Decisions made while building the documents backend (`packages/docs`, `core/documents`, migrations
`03xx`, the api documents module and the `document-git` task) against [architecture](architecture.md)
§9 and [note 11](../notes/files/11_document_versioning.md).

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DOC.1 | **Sections partition the document.** A revision's sections are contiguous and cover every code unit, so replacing one range leaves every other section byte-identical: non-blank text before the first heading is the `preamble`, each top-level heading owns its content up to the next heading of any depth (descendants are separate sections reached through `parentId`), and a document without headings is split into `block` sections of whole top-level nodes of about 4,000 characters. Structural paths are `p`, `h<n>` and `b<n>`; an id is `s` plus 25 base64url characters of `SHA-256("symplist/section/v1" ‖ commitId ‖ path)`, so ids are opaque, revision-scoped and never carry heading text. A section's content digest is its position-free mdast (its whitespace-normalized text in fallback mode), which makes a "Formatting normalized" commit content-neutral. Sections pair across revisions by continuity key (kind, depth and folded heading text; content for blocks): equal content first, then in order when the counts agree, otherwise conservative removed and added. | Build default | Architecture §9.1, §9.3; note 06 |
| DOC.2 | **Document parser work limits and a line-scanner fallback.** Chat's `SafeMarkdown` limits apply per blank-line-delimited chunk, plus a total quadratic budget (60,000,000 over the squared delimiter, backtick and bracket counts) and 20,000 container markers per document. Measured on Node 24 (`packages/docs/bench`, remark 11): a realistic 1 MiB document parses in about 1.3 s, 50,000 list items take 25.8 s and a 16-deep list tower of 5,000 lines 7.3 s, so the marker cap is what keeps parsing bounded. A document beyond the limits is indexed by a fence-aware ATX line scanner (`mode: "fallback"`), never refused, and its sections are marked approximate; it is also never re-serialized (`document.edit_invalid` for a section edit). Documents larger than 256 KiB skip the server-side canonical check (`canonical: null`); the page view computes it. | Build default | Architecture §9.1, §9.3; decision W5 |
| DOC.3 | **Git isolation beyond §9.1.** Every invocation also sets `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_ASKPASS`/`SSH_ASKPASS=/bin/false`, `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=0`, `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`, `GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_ADVICE=0`, `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` inside the workspace and `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, and the command-scope configuration adds `core.attributesFile`, `core.fsmonitor`, `core.logAllRefUpdates`, `core.pager`, `core.sshCommand=/bin/false`, an empty `credential.helper` and `diff.external`, `commit.gpgSign`, `tag.gpgSign`, `gc.auto`, `maintenance.auto`, `transfer.fsckObjects` and `init.defaultBranch` to the §9.1 four. Workspaces are `mkdtemp` directories named `symgit-*` under `GIT_TMP_DIR` (mode 0700, never a symlink), removed in `finally` and swept at startup and hourly when older than 15 minutes. Limits: 30 s and 4 MiB of output per command, 1 MiB per blob (`DOC_MAX_BYTES`), 4 MiB per diff, 64 MiB per bundle; the api runs 2 reconstructions at once with a queue of 16 and the worker 1 with a queue of 4, and a full queue is `rate.limited`. Git errors carry only a stable code, the subcommand and the exit status — never stderr, paths or arguments. | Build default | Architecture §9.1; research "Git plumbing" |
| DOC.4 | **Commit provenance lives in the encrypted history.** Authors are `You <you@users.symplist.invalid>`, `Simon <simon@agents.symplist.invalid>` and `MCP agent <mcp@agents.symplist.invalid>` with explicit whole-second dates, and the message is a deterministic subject ("Updated Next steps", "Added Links", "Formatting normalized", "Restored the version from …", "Created the page") followed by `Symplist-Author`, `Symplist-Kind` and, for a restore, `Symplist-Restored-From`. No model is involved. History is read with `git log --first-parent` from a pinned head and every entry is validated against that shape; a commit's generation is derived from the pinned head's generation and the page offset, so a page costs no extra D1 read. | Build default | Architecture §9.2; note 11 "Deterministic change retrieval" |
| DOC.5 | **Artifacts.** Object kinds `doc_bundle` (`bundles/<taskId>/<generation>-<writeId>`), `doc_snapshot` (`docs/<taskId>/<commitId>`) and `doc_job` (`jobs/<runId>/<toolCallId>.<in\|out>`), all format version 1 under the §4.2 object AAD, so an object copied to another owner, task, generation or commit fails to decrypt. A head snapshot is compact JSON: the Markdown plus the section index as positional arrays, with ids, children and continuity keys re-derived on load rather than trusted. Processes cache only ciphertext (an LRU of 64 MiB over immutable keys), so nothing decrypts without the account key the caller's authorized batch read. A snapshot upload that finds an existing object for the same commit verifies it and keeps it. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §4.2, §9.2 |
| DOC.6 | **Publication requests are fingerprinted with an encrypted digest.** `doc_publish_requests` stores `SHA-256` of the canonical request input as a field envelope (purpose `doc_request_fingerprint`), because `IDEMPOTENCY_SECRET` is api-only (§4.5) and Simon's document writes run in the worker. Scopes are `save`, `restore`, `simon:<runId>` (request id = tool call id) and `mcp:<grantId>`; rows are kept 7 days and swept hourly. A save costs two D1 requests: one read batch (task, access, key, head, request) and the publication batch. Identical content publishes nothing (`unchanged`). When the deciding statement applies nothing although the task, access and base still hold, a caller guard refused the write (a retired executor generation, a revoked grant) and the result is `document.read_only`, never a conflict. An unknown batch outcome is reconciled by request id and then the identical batch is sent once more; uploads older than 30 minutes are never published, so orphan collection can never delete an object a slow publication is about to reference. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §9.2; note 11 steps 1–7 |
| DOC.7 | **The HTTP idempotency record is folded into the publication batch and removed again when the publication loses.** `POST …/document/commits` and `…/document/restore` are `@Idempotent({ folded: true })`: the claim statements lead the batch, the claim guards the head update, the completion records the response, and a final statement deletes the record in the same batch when the head write id is not present — so a lost race answers 409 `document.conflict` and the key stays usable, while an exact retry replays the recorded 201. `unchanged` and replayed publications run a fold-only batch so the claim is always completed. Drafts (`PUT`/`DELETE …/document/draft`) take no `Idempotency-Key`: they are ordered and idempotent by `clientSeq`, like preference writes. | Build default | Architecture §6.1; decision CZ.11 |
| DOC.8 | **Drafts and conflict review.** Draft writes are throttled to one per task every 2 seconds per api process (`rate.limited` with `Retry-After`), stored encrypted with `client_seq` ordering (an older sequence is `document.draft_stale`), and cleared by the save they cover inside its batch. A conflicting save keeps its candidate as the draft with `origin = 'conflict'` unless a newer draft is stored, and answers `document.conflict` with `currentRevision`, `currentGeneration` and `draftPreserved`. `GET …/document/conflict` classifies every section as `both_changed`, `saved_changed`, `draft_changed` or `unchanged` against the draft's base and returns the two texts only for contested sections, within 128 KiB. | Build default | Architecture §9.2, §9.3; document_history brief |
| DOC.9 | **Orphan collection and maintenance.** Unreferenced bundles and snapshots are collected only when older than a one-hour grace period and after a fresh D1 reachability read: a snapshot is kept while any `doc_commits` row names it, and a bundle while it is the head bundle, within the last three published generations, or superseded less than the grace period ago (every bundle holds the complete history, so collecting a superseded one loses none). Job objects under `u/<ownerId>/jobs/` older than 24 hours go too. Passes are bounded (200 deletions, 10 list pages per prefix, 50 owners), expired publication requests and read receipts older than 30 days are deleted in batches of 500, and stale Git workspaces are swept. The api's local scheduler runs it at :35 when `DURABLE=false`; `DURABLE=true` uses the new `documents-maintenance` schedule (`d1` queue, micro, `35 * * * *`), which the integrator may fold into `cleanup-hourly` when that task exists. | Build default | Architecture §8.8, §9.2; note 11 step 7 |
| DOC.10 | **Tool bounds and revisions.** Outline 50 entries (max 100), search 10 matches (max 20) with 240-character snippets, `read_section` 8 KiB (256 B to 16 KiB), diff 16 KiB (512 B to 32 KiB), changes 50 (max 100), history 20 (max 50) and 64,000 characters per section update; callers may only lower these. A turn may retrieve 96,000 bytes of document text and an MCP grant 256,000 bytes per 10 minutes (kept in api memory, keyed by grant id); a read that cannot deliver its minimum is `document.budget_exhausted`. `task_document_read_section` names the revision its section id belongs to and reports `isHead`, so an agent may re-read a baseline excerpt; cursors bound to the head are refused with `document.stale_cursor` once it moves, and a cursor for another revision, section, query or task is `document.cursor_invalid`. `task_document_update_section` takes `placement` `replace`, `after` or `end` (so an empty page can be written), canonicalizes the replacement and keeps blank-line separation, leaving descendants and every other section byte-identical. Simon may write only from its own task chat, quick chat is read-only, and MCP needs `tasks:write` and the task in its scope. | Build default | Architecture §8.7, §9.4, §14.6; note 06 |
| DOC.11 | **Read receipts and positions.** A receipt records the delivered range of one section at one commit for one reader (conversation or grant) in a context epoch, is inserted only for published commits of the owner's task, and is idempotent by that key; tools return receipt drafts that Simon writes with its checkpoint, and MCP writes them with its response. Read positions load at most 500 receipts and the section indexes of at most 8 revisions and report `read`, `partially_read`, `changed_since_read`, `previously_read` (an earlier epoch) or `unread` per head section, plus sections read earlier that no longer exist. Receipts older than 30 days are deleted. | Build default | Architecture §9.4; note 11 "Simon's read position" |
| DOC.12 | **`document-git` payloads carry ids only.** The task resolves the owner from `tasks`, reads the encrypted job input (whose run and tool call must match the payload), runs the operation with the input's trusted actor and an executor-generation guard, and writes the encrypted output; a retried attempt reuses a completed output and publications are idempotent by tool call id. Retryable failures (`rate.limited`, D1 or storage unavailability, `git.busy`, `git.timeout`) are rethrown so Trigger retries; everything else becomes a code in the output object. Head changes reach the api as the signed internal event `document.head_changed`, and the api re-reads the head from D1 before publishing it on the `user` topic. | Build default | Architecture §6.2, §8.3, §8.8, §9.1 |
| DOC.13 | **Documents error codes**: `document.conflict` 409, `document.resync_required` 409, `document.stale_cursor` 409, `document.cursor_invalid` 400, `document.too_large` 413, `document.history_too_large` 413, `document.integrity_failed` 500, `document.budget_exhausted` 429, `document.draft_stale` 409, `document.edit_invalid` 422 and `document.read_only` 403. Unknown and foreign tasks, revisions and sections all answer the common `not_found`; a reused request id with other input answers `idempotency.mismatch`. | Build default | Architecture §6, §9 |
| DOC.14 | **The documents purge contributor deletes D1 rows only.** Receipts, publication requests, drafts, commits and repositories are deleted children-first in bounded batches, with a commit removed once no request or receipt references it and a repository once its commits are gone, so the foreign keys hold whatever order D1 applies. The encrypted bundles, snapshots and job objects live under `u/<userId>/` and are already removed by the purge's R2 step, which runs before the D1 step. | Build default | Architecture §5.6 |
| DOC.15 | **Benchmark (note 11 "measure cold and warm latency").** `packages/docs/bench/history.bench.ts`, run with `pnpm --filter @symplist/docs exec vitest run --config vitest.bench.config.ts`, measures representative histories against real Git, local SQLite and the filesystem store. On Git 2.50.1, Node 24.15.0, darwin/arm64 (cold = empty ciphertext cache): a 2.4 KB page with 28 commits has an 8.7 KB bundle and publishes in 191 ms cold / 192 ms warm, history (20 entries) 174/146 ms, diff 156 ms, snapshot read 0.3/0.0 ms; the same page with 203 commits has a 61 KB bundle and publishes in 236/216 ms, history 161/158 ms; a 58 KB page with 53 commits has a 31 KB bundle and publishes in 242/246 ms, history 161/160 ms, index build 31 ms; a 581 KB page with 23 commits has a 79 KB bundle, a 639 KB snapshot, publishes in 536/523 ms, history 209/196 ms, diff 218 ms and builds its index in 226 ms. Publication cost is dominated by the ~12 Git processes per commit (slower behind macOS's `/usr/bin/git` shim than in the Debian images), and the ciphertext cache saves a download rather than Git work. The full-bundle format therefore stays well inside the 64 MiB bundle limit for beta-sized histories; incremental bundles are still the migration path if a page's history outgrows it. | Build default | Note 11 "R2: encrypted Git artifacts" |
| DOC.16 | **Platform fixes and a dependency.** `packages/db/src/migrations.test.ts` and `schema.test.ts` asserted that every migration file is in the foundation range and that the applied schema is exactly the foundation tables, which any feature migration broke; they now check that every file is inside a declared owner range and that the foundation's tables are all present and `STRICT`. `@types/mdast` 4.0.4 is a new dev dependency of `@symplist/docs` (mdast types for the section parser). `packages/docs/src/test-support/` and `packages/core/src/documents/test-support.ts` build the local drivers, users, tasks and account keys the document tests share. | Build default | Architecture §3.4, §17 |
| DOC.17 | **The page view is Milkdown and the Markdown view is CodeMirror, and the pane decides which one a document may use.** `page-view.tsx` is Milkdown over the same Markdown string the CodeMirror `raw-view.tsx` edits, so R7's one "Formatting normalized" commit is the only formatting change a reader ever sees; `page-view.test.tsx` asserts that a canonical document — including the research's hostile round-trip document, minus its raw HTML — reaches Milkdown and comes back unchanged. A document that is only line-scanned (`parseMode: 'fallback'`) now reports `too_complex` rather than `raw_html`: a fallback head cannot know about HTML, so it says `hasRawHtml: true` conservatively, and checking the parser's own limit first is the only way the notice tells the truth. | Build default | Architecture §9.3; Phase A research; progress note 2026-09-16 |
| DOC.18 | **A toolbar command reports what the document says, not what the editor's command dispatch returns.** Milkdown's `callCommand` answers `false` for commands it did apply, and a command that applies can still throw on the way out when scrolling the caret into view finds no layout. `runToolbarCommand` therefore compares the editor state before and after — a new document, or a new set of stored marks for an inline mark toggled with nothing selected — and reports that. `jsdom-layout.ts` is a documents-local test helper giving `Range`, `Element` and `Text` the zero-sized client rects both editors need; it is deliberately not added to the shared `apps/web/vitest.setup.ts`, which several feature branches edit at once. | Build default | Architecture §9.3; task_document brief |
| DOC.19 | **"Artifacts and links" is a documents frame with a sharing body.** `/tasks/:taskId/artifacts` is owned by the documents feature: Back to page, the version a link would capture (from the documents head), the way on to revisions, and the plain statements that later edits never change a link already created and that opening the screen creates nothing. The list of snapshots and grants belongs to sharing (§13, wave D2) and arrives through `artifact-surface.ts`, registered the way Simon registers its outline handler; until then the screen shows "No links yet" and says sharing is not available in this build, rather than offering controls that would do nothing. The standalone read-only artifact viewer (artifact_viewer.md) is not a Next route at all — §13.2 and §13.4 serve it from the api on `ARTIFACT_ORIGIN` with no scripts — so it stays entirely with the sharing feature. | Build default | Architecture §2.3, §13; artifact_shares.md, artifact_share.md, artifact_viewer.md |
| DOC.20 | **A save that owes only a normalization publishes only that.** Review of the documents web stage found that a blur, Mod+S or task switch on an untouched non-canonical page in the page view published "Formatting normalized" and then immediately published the buffer — still holding the old formatting — as an edit that reverted it, leaving the head non-canonical with `normalizationPending` cleared. `runSave` now finishes after the normalization when nothing local is unsaved, the reducer's `normalization_published` carries an untouched buffer forward to the canonical text, and the normalization's idempotency key is scoped to the revision it rewrites (`normalize:<revision>`) so a key kept for a retry is never reused across heads. `resolveConflict` reports `stillDirty` from the buffer, like `runSave`, instead of assuming nothing was typed while the merge published. | Code review | DOC.17, DOC.18; architecture §6.1, §9.3; decision R7 |
| DOC.21 | **The history screen carries focus between its two phone screens, and its detail panel ignores stale answers.** At the phone breakpoint the stylesheet hides whichever of the revisions list and the preview is off-screen, so the focused control was removed from the page and focus fell to `<body>`; opening a revision now focuses the preview region and returning focuses the selected revision again, which is what the existing `tabIndex={-1}` and `:focus { outline: none }` were for. Every detail write is gated on a request token, so two revisions opened in quick succession show the one asked for last whichever answer arrives first. A locked page states its reason in the Markdown view too, rather than presenting a silently uneditable editor. | Code review | Architecture §9.3; document_history.md, task_document.md, system_states.md |

## Phase D1 merge

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | **The tasks domain is the single writer of archive search intents.** `tasks/plans.ts` records one `search_intents` upsert per task a completion archived *and* per subtask `parent_only` promoted into its place, in the deciding batch, guarded by `tasks.write_id`. `searchArchiveContributor` was written against an earlier shape of the archive seam, carried its own guard rather than `archiveGuard(input)` — which made the runner refuse it and every `POST /v1/tasks/:id/complete` answer 500 — and would have written every archived task's intent a second time, since `search_intents` rows carry no unique key. The contributor keeps its place in the seam's batch order and contributes nothing; the seam forbids a contributor from writing `tasks` at all, so it could not have narrowed its insert to the rows the plan misses. | Build default | S5; §2.1, §10.1 |
| M2 | **`packages/contracts` imports `z` only from `common/zod.ts`, in every feature.** The search, access and documents branches each added schema modules importing `"zod"` directly. The browser's CSP has no `unsafe-eval`, so that module's `jitless` configuration has to be settled before any schema is built, and a bundler concatenates modules in import order. Five files repointed; `common/zod.test.ts` was not touched. | Build default | WS merge note 2; §5.3, decision W1 |
| M3 | **The palette places recent tasks from the owner's tree, not one read per id.** `createSearchApi.recentTasks` resolved up to eight recent ids with eight parallel `GET /v1/tasks/:id` every time the palette opened on an empty query — two dozen requests for three openings in ten seconds, against a 2 req/s lane. It now walks `GET /v1/tasks` one bounded page per collection, stops the moment every id is placed and reads at most `RECENT_TREE_PAGE_BUDGET` (4) pages; the api serves them all from the one owner tree it caches for 60 s, so the usual opening is one request over one D1 read. An archived or removed id is simply not in the tree, which is how it drops out. | Build default | §3.1, §3.3; S11 |
| M4 | **One admin invite search costs at most five D1 requests.** `InviteAdminService.list` read 200 rows at a time and loaded a key ring per page — ten of each for a large table. It reads at most four 500-row pages and loads one key ring for all of them, and stops early once enough rows have matched on `hint` or `bound_email`, the fields that need no key. A label is encrypted, so it can only match after decryption; reach, order and the continuation cursor are unchanged. | Build default | §3.1; AC review |
| M5 | **A spec that is not about access stubs the identity, and nothing else.** Every `(app)` route sits behind the proxy's session-hint redirect (§5.1) and `SessionGate`'s `GET /v1/me` check (§5.4). `shell.spec.ts` asserts the shell with the api refusing every read and `search.spec.ts` runs against contract-shaped fixtures; both now get the hint cookie and one admitted identity from `apps/e2e/src/helpers/identity.ts`, and leave every other read to fail or to their own fixtures. `access.spec.ts` owns both gates end to end. | Build default | §5.1, §5.4; S16 |
| M6 | **One environment starts the end-to-end api.** `apps/e2e/src/helpers/local-api.ts` owns it, including `NODE_ENV=test` (without which the test-only OTP outbox does not exist and no access journey can read an emailed code, decision AC12) and `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL`. `access.spec.ts` used to spawn an api of its own with a second environment; once the workspace feature gave the whole suite one through Playwright's `webServer`, the two had to agree and did not. The spec's private launcher is gone and it waits for the shared api instead. | Build default | AC12; §16.1, §17 |
| BR1 | **The mark carries no colour of its own.** Three rows on a 24-unit grid, line lengths stepping down 11.0 / 7.4 / 3.8 by a constant 3.6, stroke 2.2, round caps, drawn in `currentColor`. The app ships six themes in light and dark with a user-chosen accent, so a mark with a fixed colour would fight at least one of them. The wordmark is lowercase, as the product notes write it, and pinned to Geist rather than the active theme's `--sym-font`: a wordmark is an identity and must not change with the theme. The favicon and app icon are the knockout-on-ink variant, because the bare mark's three rows close up below 16 px; the Android maskable icon is a separate file that shrinks the mark into the centre 80% safe zone, since reusing the standard icon would let the crop clip the outer dots. | Owner asked for a black and white logo | Brief `themes.md`, `overall.md` |
| BR2 | **The share card is a committed PNG, not a generated `opengraph-image`.** Rendered once at 1200×630 and 1200×600 with the real Geist face, so a link preview never depends on a font fetch or a render at request time. `metadataBase` comes from the public web origin so a preview never resolves to localhost, and `robots` is `index: false` because the workspace is private. | Build default | Architecture §10.3 |
| WS25 | **Quick add has two saving keys.** Enter adds the task and moves focus to it, so the next keystroke acts on what was just made; Shift + Enter adds it and keeps the caret in the field for the next one. The pair is only worth having because the two differ: a single Enter that both saved and stayed left no way to say "done". A failed add returns no id and leaves focus in the field beside the draft it restored. Both are handled on `keydown` rather than through the form's submit so they can be told apart, and an Enter raised while an IME is composing is ignored so it commits a candidate instead of adding a task. The field names both keys visibly and through `aria-describedby`. | Owner request | Note 13; brief `workspace_now.md` |

## Phase E — Environment distribution

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ENV1 | **Environment distribution follows the binding §4.5 inventory, not the root template's obsolete “all 12 shared” sentence.** The api receives all twelve generated families; the worker receives only `CONTENT_KEK`, `INTERNAL_EVENT_SECRET` and `REMINDER_UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET`, with identical versions and values. A durable api omits AI provider credentials, the worker file always omits platform-injected `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY`, and the web receives only its five public/build variables. `pnpm env:distribute` derives the placement from the checked-in app templates and inventory, validates all three runtime schemas before atomic mode-600 writes, and `pnpm env:check` verifies the resulting ignored files without printing values. | Phase E implementation; resolves conflicting owner shorthand and root-template prose in favor of binding architecture/config | Architecture §4.5, §16.1–16.2; decision C1.7 |

## Phase D2 — Simon

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SI1 | **Connector read exemptions start empty.** Provider `readOnlyHint` alone cannot establish a reviewed action. An exemption must pin the canonical schema hash and exact selector argument paths; unknown strings, destination/recipient fields, URLs and email-like values require approval even on a reviewed action. Schema drift or missing hints returns to approval. Sandbox and upstream meta execution slugs are unavailable even if discovery returns them. | Build default | §8.4–8.5; note 12 |
| SI2 | **Message acceptance has a bounded durable queue and an encrypted retry fingerprint.** Each conversation assigns monotonically increasing integer sequence numbers in its deciding update, accepts at most 20 queued follow-ups and limits one submitted message to 32,000 characters. The unique `(conversation_id, request_id)` record reconciles a lost response; its SHA-256 over canonical validated text/tier is itself encrypted under the account key. Exact retries never extend quick-chat expiry or add another run. The eventual HTTP surface must additionally fold the platform idempotency claim into its acceptance batch. | Build default | §3.1–3.2, §6.1, §8.1 |
| SI3 | **Simon history references bind resource and owner together.** Migration 0500 uses composite foreign keys for tasks, conversations, messages and runs, plus a partial unique index allowing one queued/running/paused run per conversation. `active_run_id` remains an application-guarded claim to avoid a cyclic insert dependency. Purge deletes bounded childless rows so continuation and superseded-approval references remain valid between batches. Every claim also requires an existing account key, preventing a claimed-but-unreadable run after crypto-shred. | Build default | §4, §5.6, §8.1 |
| SI4 | **A confirmed connection is required before an approval can exist.** Migration 0900 introduces the minimal owner/toolkit/upstream-account mapping ahead of the connections UI, without storing OAuth tokens or connector catalogues. The same deciding-statement guard checks its active status and generation when pausing and claiming an external action. Reconnecting even the same upstream account increments the generation. Migration 0501 adds a nullable approval generation; legacy rows dual-read as generation 1. Connection creation, reconciliation and provider revocation remain D2e work. | Build default | §8.4, §14.1–14.2 |
| SI5 | **A pause and its resolution own the conversation atomically.** Approval and question contents are encrypted in the assistant checkpoint batch. Approve, deny, dismiss, answer and expiry condition on the original active paused run, owner, admission, task state and expiry; only one creates the continuation, ahead of queued chat messages and at the current executor generation. A chat reply never resolves a pause. Both pause types expire after 24 hours; a generation-fenced sweep considers at most 25 eligible expired pauses per pass. HTTP idempotency will be folded into these batches when the routes land. | Build default | §6.1, §8.1, §8.4, §8.7 |
| SI6 | **Editing an approval draft requests a new review.** Only a trusted tool-catalogue validator can validate edited arguments and rebuild the preview/policy version. The old approval becomes superseded and the new encrypted draft receives its own digest and expiry, without dispatching. The user must approve that new digest. An account change or reconnect during validation refuses the replacement. | Build default | §8.4; agent_approval brief |
| SI7 | **The side-effect ledger is never a stealable lease.** A conditional durable `started` record precedes the no-retry provider call. A duplicate or process loss with no recorded result reports `uncertain`, never resends, and only a known saved result is replayable. Provider exceptions are discarded rather than persisting their potentially private text. A requested Stop may still record an already-completed effect; restriction, task archive or executor-generation change fences its result write. | Build default | §8.4; note 07 |
| SI8 | **Lifecycle reconciliation uses the same queue advancement as a normal finish.** Simon now supplies the registered tracker and output relay source. Heartbeats batch at most 90 ids per statement, old-generation running work cannot be rebound by a late dispatch acknowledgement, and interruption never replaces a terminal checkpoint. Queue advancement checks the configured beta-admission policy, including self-hosting with the beta gate disabled. | Build default | §3.1, §8.1–8.3 |
| D2P.1 | **D2 uses isolated single-writer worktrees with the architecture's existing migration allocations.** The owner's latest instruction supersedes the earlier single-checkout restriction. The suggested 0300–0499 numbers overlap Documents/Search; preserve §3.4's 05xx Simon, 06xx Scheduling, 07xx Vault, 08xx Sharing, 09xx Connections and 10xx Analytics ranges instead. Connections extends existing 0900. Each stream reports shared-file changes, appends its own CSS block, and lands separately after Simon with a typecheck and loss audit. | Owner parallelization instruction; collision resolved from repository evidence | §3.4; docs/build/d2-parallel.md |
| SI9 | **The shared loop owns encrypted structured snapshots and pause publication.** AI SDK callback exceptions are not sufficient to stop execution, so checkpoint failures explicitly abort the loop. Pending approval/question output waits until its encrypted pause and complete tool-result checkpoint commit; ordinary output is flushed while the run remains active. The relay accepts paused runs so a committed pause card can arrive afterwards. Queued user messages receive a fresh sequence when advanced, preserving user/assistant chronology. SDK telemetry and content-bearing warnings are disabled; model/tool exceptions crossing Trigger carry stable codes only. | Build default | §8.1–8.6 |
| SI10 | **A document receipt proves a checkpointed tool result, not merely a successful read.** A turn stages receipts by tool-call id and folds only those whose output-available parts are in the encrypted snapshot into the same deciding batch. Stop between read completion and the step boundary records no false receipt. Owner, conversation, run and write-id guards bind every receipt; retrieved bytes are bounded by the existing 96,000-byte turn budget. Document-derived titles, headings, snippets and results use escaped untrusted-data delimiters; the initial context includes identity/title/revision/read positions, never the document body. | Build default | §8.5, §8.7, §9.4 |
| SI11 | **Document child jobs retain the exact live parent claim.** Generation alone cannot fence Stop. The encrypted job actor must match the running parent's owner, conversation, task, kind, context epoch, active claim and executor generation; cancellation is checked both before work and inside the final Git publication guard. Durable Simon routes every Git operation through encrypted job objects and `triggerAndWait`; its local Git runner explicitly refuses execution. The API shares one infrastructure-owned two-slot Git service across core-service callers, without importing another feature's Nest module. | Build default | §2.3, §8.8, §9.1; R6 |
| SI12 | **Chat HTTP writes fold their recorded result into the deciding transaction.** Creation, message acceptance, Stop and Retry use the platform claim without a separate post-effect response write. Message acceptance prepares encrypted accepted/queued alternatives; only the actual guarded outcome completes the claim. A refused write deletes only its own pending claim. Persisted message request ids keep deduplicating even after the 24-hour response record expires, extending SI2's lost-response guarantee; a changed message under that id remains a mismatch. Fresh authorization also gates replay after the preparation read. | Build default | §3.1, §6.1, §8.1; SI2 |
| SI13 | **Explicit Retry forms a linear continuation chain and cannot displace active work.** Only a stopped, failed or interrupted predecessor with no existing child and an idle, admitted, active conversation can create a retry. The new run uses the current executor generation and retains the applicable approval/question reference. Its action ledger returns saved or uncertain outcomes without another external call; snapshot resolution binds to that exact pause rather than assuming it is the retry's direct parent. After another interruption the UI retries the latest child. Stop's durable flag commits before best-effort executor cancellation, and exact HTTP retries safely attempt cancellation again. | Build default | §8.1, §8.4; SI7 |

## Phase D2 — Connections and incoming MCP

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
