| D2E.1 | **External actions execute individually with a documented explicit account selector.** The Symplist `execute_tools` wrapper resolves each action through confirmed D1 ownership and trusted SDK toolkit metadata. Composio 0.18.1 documents `session.execute(actionSlug, args, {account})` but says meta tools may ignore that top-level selector. Use direct session execution for each resolved action, with `getClient().withOptions({maxRetries:0}).toolRouter.session.execute` for writes, instead of trusting an undocumented nested selector in `COMPOSIO_MULTI_EXECUTE_TOOL`. The outer Symplist batch/approval policy and invocation ledger remain authoritative; no multi-execute, workbench or sandbox endpoint is exposed. | Build default | §14.1, note 12 wrapper mapping; exact-account approval binding |
| D2E.2 | **Session pins have a durable update lease and generation.** Migration 0901 adds one session row per owner, a 60-second fenced pin-update lease and a connection-state generation advanced by insert/update/delete triggers. A lost connection generation, admission, account key or lease refuses publication; newly created unpublished sessions are deleted best-effort. Only a definitive upstream 404 recreates a session. A transient failure never creates a replacement. Catalogue pages are cached for two minutes in memory only, with cycle/page limits and no storage dependency. | Build default | §3.1, §14.1–14.3 |
| D2E.3 | **Provider logs are disabled at both Composio layers.** Core's exported logger has no configuration setter and can log content; its methods are explicitly replaced with a silent sink before client construction. The raw client's logger is the same silent sink and logLevel is off, inherited by no-retry clones. Symplist runtimes log only the normalized integration code. A test exercises the installed raw client's failed execution with a private marker and asserts no console calls. | Build default | §6.3, §8.3, §14.1 |
| SI14 | **Additional actor authority belongs inside Simon's transaction, including replay.** `SimonWriteFold.authorization` accepts trusted core SQL with isolated `simon_auth_` bind names; it cannot shadow or borrow the mutation's identity parameters. Creation and message acceptance, and the shared lifecycle mutations, require it in their deciding writes and before returning a recorded response. `SimonRepository.run` applies the same optional predicate to its read. The incoming MCP adapter supplies the grant generation, owner, scope and task restriction; HTTP app callers do not accept this predicate from clients. This seam is not itself an implemented MCP server. | Build default | §3.1, §6.1, §14.4–14.6 |
| D2E.4 | **Connection attempt nonces use the existing API-only CSRF digest family.** Store `version.digest` from `HMAC(SESSION_DIGEST_SECRET, 'csrf' || NUL || 'connection-attempt' || NUL || attemptId || NUL || nonce)`, and check all configured versions in the deciding callback statement. The 32-byte nonce and provider attestation/link tokens are never persisted. The nested domain separation cannot collide with the ordinary session-id CSRF input. This adds no secret family and keeps callback creation/confirmation out of the worker. | Build default | §4.3, §5.3, §14.2 |
| D2E.5 | **Hosted connection creation uses the SDK's raw no-retry clone.** Core `ComposioRequestOptions` does not accept retry options. Raw `link.create` sends the exact hosted-link fields used by `connectedAccounts.link` with `allowMultiple:true` (that flag disables an SDK-only preflight; it is not a wire field). Auth-config creation uses the same no-retry clone and a 15-second timeout, inside the toolkit's 60-second D1 lease. The missing SDK `complete_auth` call uses a fixed Composio URL; `session_uri` is only a body token, never a fetched URL. At most five live connect attempts and 500 connection records per account bound lifecycle work. | Build default | §3.1, §14.2–14.3 |
| D2E.6 | **Connection changes expire approvals with set-based continuations, not an approval-count cutoff.** Five fixed-size statements expire every pending approval behind the deciding connection write, finish eligible paused runs, insert continuations at the current executor generation, transfer each conversation and insert dispatch intents. The approval UUIDv7 is reused as its continuation run id and dispatch id in those separate table namespaces; retries are deterministic and cannot duplicate a continuation. Access, active task, cancellation, conversation ownership and expiry still gate continuation creation. A 100-approval test verifies constant statement/bind counts. Provider revocation is an ids-only durable cleanup job committed with native disconnect; an outage cannot restore native authority. | Build default | §3.1–3.2, §8.4, §14.2–14.3 |
| D2E.7 | **Reconciliation protects the callback's bounded attestation window.** Unconfirmed ACTIVE accounts are durably queued for deletion only when no live pending/completing attempt names them; cleanup claims recheck both that condition and confirmed native authority. Otherwise a daily scan concurrent with a valid callback could destroy the account before publication. The ten-minute attempt expiry bounds this exemption. Reconciliation applies at most eight connection changes per D1 batch and claims at most twenty provider revocations per pass; deciding writes include the executor mode/generation. Provider purge rereads the first shrinking page in twenty-account passes, then deletes the known session without using an account key. | Build default | §3.1, §5.6, §8.1, §14.2–14.3 |
| D2E.8 | **MCP API keys use the same thirty-day absolute lifetime as OAuth grants.** Key creation permits at most 100 active grants per owner and 100 explicitly selected tasks, checked for active ownership in the deciding transaction with `json_each` rather than a variable bind list. Labels are encrypted, raw keys are returned once and never placed in even encrypted idempotency responses; the platform records a redacted placeholder response. Grant listings put every active grant before bounded recent history. The grant's generation, expiry, permission and selected-task predicate is exported under isolated task/Simon bind namespaces for integration in their actual deciding writes and replay checks. | Build default | §3.1–3.2, §6.1, §14.4–14.6 |
| SI14 | **Additional actor authority belongs inside Simon's transaction, including replay.** `SimonWriteFold.authorization` accepts trusted core SQL with isolated `simon_auth_` bind names; it cannot shadow or borrow the mutation's identity parameters. Creation and message acceptance, and the shared lifecycle mutations, require it in their deciding writes and before returning a recorded response. `SimonRepository.run` applies the same optional predicate to its read. The incoming MCP adapter supplies the grant generation, owner, scope and task restriction; HTTP app callers do not accept this predicate from clients. This seam is not itself an implemented MCP server. | Build default | §3.1, §6.1, §14.4–14.6 |
| SI15 | **Approval HTTP decisions require fresh session authority and a folded result.** Preparation reads approval, run, account key and confirmed connection in one batch; the deciding batch records the exact decision or fresh-review replacement together with its encrypted idempotency response. A refused effect leaves no pending claim. Exact replay still checks admission, account key, conversation expiry and active task. The owner route bypasses the session cache and folds session revocation into its write/replay guard. Approve rechecks the original account generation even when arguments were not edited. | Build default; adversarial review fixed cached-session and archived-task replay gaps | §3.3, §6.1, §8.4 |
| SI16 | **Edited-draft validation is metadata-only in the API.** The deterministic policy has an explicit `@symplist/agent/policy` export that imports no model or executor. Connections supplies an authenticated-owner-bound schema/preview validator through a factory; until that integration lands the optional seam fails closed on edits. Validation never executes the proposed tool, resolves a Vault secret or turns the edited draft into an approval. | Build default | §8.4–8.5; durable executor boundary |
| SI17 | **Public conversation history is a bounded projection, not model continuation state.** Each owner-authorized read transaction returns at most 50 messages within a 2 MiB encrypted payload budget, paged by message sequence, and strips reasoning, provider metadata and raw tool inputs. Only text, projected tool outcomes and the two first-party resolution data parts are exposed. Reconnect snapshots include only the active run's newest contiguous live tail, capped at 256 KiB with an explicit truncation flag; client reduction must reconcile by run/message identity rather than concatenate saved text and deltas. An authoritative denial during snapshot loading detaches the subscription and discards queued frames, unlike a transient outage. | Build default; adversarial review | §3.1, §7, §8.2; task_chat and agent_approval briefs |
| D2V.1 | **Vault wraps have an outer account-key envelope.** The Argon2 passphrase wrap, service-recovery wrap and token-derived session wrap are each stored inside a normal account-key field envelope. A bare recovery wrapper would survive account-key deletion and contradict R12. Items use the frozen Vault-item AAD under the random Vault data key; grant values use the frozen grant AAD under the account key. | Build default | §4.1–4.2, §5.6, §11; R12 |
| D2V.2 | **Sensitive drafts are memory-only and discarded on lock.** The editor warns before editing that inactivity, a hidden tab, reset or explicit lock clears its plaintext and draft. The browser renders the unlock surface instead of a blurred item list. No local/session storage or query cache contains Vault items. Hidden tabs lock early; returning never silently unlocks. | Build default | vault_item_editor, vault_unlock; §11.1 |
| D2V.3 | **A Vault key defaults to a 12-character NFKC phrase policy, configurable through the Vault service options and returned by the status contract.** The existing shared Argon2 implementation enforces its fixed work factor and two-slot semaphore; no verifier hash of the derived wrapping key is stored. HTTP input is bounded before work. | Build default | vault_setup; §4.3, §11.1 |
| D2V.4 | **Vault grant argument paths are JSON Pointers.** Exact pointers include array indices and escaped slash/tilde segments, reject prototype keys and never treat a dot as a separator. Resolution accepts at most 20 handles and only task conversations, and returns a mandatory redactor alongside the resolved arguments for the executor to use before any result sink. | Build default | §11.3 |
| D2V.5 | **Security OTP delivery is shared infrastructure, not a feature-module import.** Access and Vault both use core OtpService through the platform's email providers, preserving the existing token names, purpose-bound challenges, provider retry key and test-only OTP outbox. Vault reset notices have a redacted audit-backed retry queue in the api with one stable provider key; no new Trigger task or plaintext content sink is introduced. | Build default | §2.3, §5.1, §11.2 |
| D2V.6 | **Vault lists use 15-item pages and a 16th-row cursor probe.** Each item's encrypted JSON can contain a 64,000-character note; JSON escaping followed by envelope base64 makes a 100-row query exceed D1's 10 MiB response ceiling. Sixteen worst-case rows stay below that ceiling. Unlocked list search is explicitly within loaded items, with load-more pagination; no Vault content enters a general search index. | Build default; adversarial sizing review | §3, §11.2 |
| D2C.1 | **A schedule is one optimistic-versioned snapshot with at most twenty explicit reminders.** Saving cancels prior pending occurrences and increments reminder generations in the deciding batch; replacing a deadline never changes task identity, collection or Markdown. Standalone reminders use their own IANA zone. Date-only deadlines store the date and zone, with the next local-day instant only as an operational overdue boundary. DST gaps and repeated local times require an explicit earlier/later choice. | Build default | §12.1; task_schedule brief; note 15 |
| D2C.2 | **Provider delivery events have a bounded-content-free correlation ledger.** A Resend webhook can arrive before the send response's provider id is persisted. Migration 0601 adds only provider id, status, event time and receipt ids, plus a nullable receipt write id; reconciliation applies the newest verified event after acceptance catches up. Raw provider bodies, subjects and bounce messages are never stored. Only a Permanent bounce or complaint adds a versioned address-digest suppression. | Build default | §12.5; R14 |
| D2C.3 | **Deadline chips read visible tasks in batches of at most fifty.** Unmounted chips leave the store; reconnect refreshes only mounted ids serially. Opening an editor reads the full schedule. This avoids both one-request-per-row mounting and the D1 reconnect fan-out found in D1 review. | Build default | §3.1; task_schedule brief |
| D2C.4 | **Delivery-event reconciliation lives in the API, where the optional webhook secret belongs.** A non-overlapping minute timer reconciles at most 100 content-free provider correlations only when `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is configured. Worker cleanup never infers webhook availability or receives that secret. With tracking disabled, Settings hides suppression health and accepted/uncertain rows remain unchanged by reconciliation. | Build default | §12.5; R14; secret-placement matrix |
| D2C.5 | **Scheduling operation retries replay before re-planning.** An encrypted immutable operation fingerprint and encrypted response (nullable expand-only `schedule_audit.response_enc`) prevent add/cancel/snooze retries from acting again on the state they already changed. Trusted executor/grant guards apply to both replay authorization and the deciding schedule write. | Adversarial review | §6.1; §8.7; §12.1 |
| D2C.6 | **Channel opt-out removes that channel from pending reminder definitions as well as cancelling its outbox rows.** Mixed-channel reminders retain their still-enabled channel; reminders with no channels become cancelled. Affected schedule versions advance so a stale editor cannot silently restore cancelled settings. Re-enabling a preference never resurrects earlier deliveries. | Adversarial review | §12.4; settings_notifications brief |
| D2C.7 | **A scan batches concurrent database phases and coalesces UI hints by owner.** At most fifty occurrences are claimed, at most five provider calls run concurrently, and each logical claim/write plan remains contiguous within the scan-scoped D1 batching adapter. One changed hint per affected owner refreshes the persisted center without a burst of individual requests or toasts. | Build default and lane review | §3.1; §12.2–12.3 |
| D2C.8 | **Timezone detection is persisted on the first admitted workspace after onboarding, only when notification preferences do not exist.** The optimistic version-zero save cannot overwrite a concurrent explicit settings change. Later device or travel timezone changes never rewrite the stored timezone or existing deadlines, and detection creates no reminder or email opt-in. | Build default | Note 15; §12.1 |
| D2D.1 | **Analytics identity stays server-side.** R9 forbids `analytics_id` in responses, which precludes §15's browser `identify(analyticsId)` flow. Browser-owned allowlisted events instead use an authenticated, CSRF-protected first-party relay; it reads current consent and the random id and sends through the existing PostHog US server emitter. No browser SDK, identity, persistence or pre-consent queue is introduced. Client/server event ownership remains unchanged. Accept and Decline have equal prominence and Settings uses the same stored consent. | Build default, confirmed by integrator | R9 overrides §15 client identity delivery; note 17 permits a server-only adapter |
| D2D.2 | **Artifact selection exports each explicitly selected section's own text, in source order.** Selecting a heading does not silently include its descendants; select those sections separately or choose the whole saved document. Snapshots read authenticated encrypted head objects, never Git. Unreleased proposals and release reviews bind to the current source head, while already released content stays immutable. | Build default | §9.2, §13.1; note 16 |
| D2D.3 | **Password capacity is reserved before Argon2id.** Durable per-grant/IP 15-minute and per-grant daily windows reserve attempts conditionally before the shared semaphore; successful verification refunds its own reservation only after a generation- and access-guarded session insert. Stateless per-render form nonces bind grant, generation, creation time and randomness for ten minutes. Raw IP addresses never enter D1. | Build default | §13.3, §5.8 |
| D2D.4 | **An interrupted snapshot publication leaves a collectible encrypted object, not an unguarded artifact row.** Snapshots finish their access/head/run-guarded publication within ten minutes; orphan collection considers at most 100 keys and only objects older than 24 hours, with one JSON-bound reference lookup. Hourly cleanup separately expires bounded proposals, sessions and limit windows. | Build default | §3.1–3.2, §4, §13.1 |
| D2D.5 | **Artifact inventories use independent keyset cursors for snapshots and grants.** Each response has at most 50 snapshots and 200 grants, with explicit completed cursors and one bounded batch. Grant-change events contain only task and artifact ids; the open owner surface coalesces bursts/reconnects into one inventory read rather than refetching every remembered grant. | Build default | §3, §7, §13 |
| D2D.6 | **The script-free artifact viewer self-hosts an allowlisted Geist font asset set.** Every response on the artifact hostname receives the privacy headers before authentication/validation; successful HTML replaces the default deny-style CSP with its exact stylesheet hash. No third-party font request, browser analytics SDK or app-shell script is loaded. | Build default | §13.2–13.4, artifact_viewer brief |
| SI18 | **Task tools carry trusted run/grant predicates through writes and replay.** `TaskAuthorization` binds use the reserved `task_auth_` namespace and cannot borrow operation binds or override owner identity. Create/move predicates execute in the deciding batch; duplicate tool results, folded replays and non-fold planning errors recheck current authority. No-op moves enumerate the whole subtree, not the public first page, and verify the exact cached tree version alongside authority before returning IDs. A stale no-op read fails closed and invalidates the cache so a retry reads current membership. Adapters bind these predicates to their authenticated run/grant and exact target/subtree scope; model arguments never supply SQL. | Build default; adversarial review | §2.1, §3.1, §6, §8.7, §14.6 |
| D2E.9 | **Consent redirects are one-time credentials.** The trusted owner decision returns the stored, validated redirect URL only once; folded idempotency removes the whole URL, including code and state, from its durable response. A lost-response replay requires restarting authorization. Consent labels and state are account-key field envelopes. `/v1/oauth/requests/*` explicitly retains its app prefix alongside the unprefixed public OAuth tree. Signed-out authorization resumes through the same-origin web `/oauth/authorize` bridge. | Build default | §4, §6.1, §14.5 |
| D2E.10 | **OAuth replay revokes only after credential bindings are proven.** Code replay first verifies the exact client, redirect, resource and S256 verifier; refresh replay verifies client and resource. Only then may the single-use CAS revoke the entire grant. Invalid bindings never consume a legitimate credential or let a wrong client revoke it. Optional token scopes must match the granted permissions before consumption; grant lifetime is absolute, never extended by rotation. | Security review | §14.4–14.5 |
| D2E.11 | **MCP mutations use grant-namespaced request IDs and actual core authorization predicates.** Task creation requires all-task scope because a newly created id cannot belong to an existing selection; moves require every affected descendant to remain selected. Response projections omit analytics identifiers and out-of-scope ancestry. Search rebuild requests feed the existing bounded coordinator, and MCP uses its own 8 MiB disposable search cache. | Build default; security review | §6, §14.6, §15 |
| D2E.12 | **MCP cross-feature calls use the existing concrete core services.** Schedule writes retain exact audit replay; snapshot retries retain the immutable artifact; share revocation folds encrypted idempotency and current grant authority into its actual deciding batch. The server derives a revoke's task from the owner's artifact row, never a client assertion. Document results are reauthorized after object/Git I/O, and concurrent grant reads may not overdraw their shared delivery budget. Only applied task writes emit server analytics. | Build default; adversarial review | §6, §9.4, §12–15 |
| D2M.1 | **Hourly cleanup retains its artifact cursor in D1, not a worker process.** Expand-only migration 0604 adds a singleton owner/object cursor with a five-minute conditional lease. Each pass considers one owner page of at most 100 keys; expiry statements affect at most 100 rows per table. The executor generation is checked inside every deciding SQL statement and before each group of at most ten R2 deletions. Already-dispatched deletion calls cannot be recalled, but only unreferenced objects older than 24 hours qualify, beyond the ten-minute publication window. The next pass resumes the persisted opaque cursor even in a new process. Search recovery is bounded to five owners per pass, with a fresh fence before each dispatch, leaving room in the seven-process D1 lane for feature cleanup. | Build default | §3.1–3.2, §8.8, §11.3, §13.1; D2D.4 |
| D2M.2 | **Vault invalidation precedes socket closure and targets only the affected socket.** Logout sends canonical `vault.locked {reason:'logout'}` before 4401; revocation/restriction sends `revoked`, and observed session expiry sends `idle`. This content-free frame bypasses an in-progress snapshot queue, whose protected data is discarded on close. It is not broadcast to unaffected login sessions of the same account. Existing owner checks, stale-upgrade fences and close codes remain unchanged. | Build default | §5.1, §5.5, §7, §11.1 |
| SI19 | **Quick-chat conversion waits until work finishes or is stopped.** Save creates a normal user task and attaches the conversation, historical runs and encrypted history in the same task write transaction. The conversation UUID is reused in the separate task-id namespace, so a lost reply cannot create another task. An active run (including pending approval/question) refuses conversion; the UI must explain that work must finish or stop first. This prevents changing an action's task identity mid-execution. Conversion advances the context epoch and removes expiry. Owner-only folded replay checks fresh access before returning the recorded result. | Build default | §6.1, §8.1, §8.7 |
| SI20 | **Closing quick chat deletes its encrypted history synchronously.** One owner-guarded transaction deletes the conversation's parts, messages, action ledger, approvals, questions, read receipts and runs, including continuation chains. The active run id is recorded with the folded close result so safe executor cancellation can repeat after a lost reply. Dispatch intents retain ids only and are cancelled, not history. Hourly cleanup deletes at most five expired conversations per pass, one transaction per conversation, with expiry and current executor generation inside every mutation. Already-dispatched external actions cannot be recalled; missing run authority prevents further checkpoints or actions. | Build default | §3.1, §6.1, §8.1, §8.7–8.8 |
| SI21 | **Simon uses adapted Vercel AI Elements presentation, not its default chat endpoint or approval transport.** Reuse the conversation/message primitives with Symplist theme tokens and existing Base UI controls; keep app REST commands, owner WebSocket replay/snapshots and Symplist approvals authoritative. Do not install unneeded attachment, model marketplace, provider reasoning or generic confirmation surfaces. Preserve upstream license notices and test accessibility, reduced motion and Strict Mode lifecycle. | Owner suggestion; package inspection | §7–8; task_chat and agent_approval briefs |
| D2M3 | **Native task replay receipts follow run lifetime, not the HTTP replay window.** Simon create/move use encrypted folded idempotency records in the private `simon.native.task` scope, keyed by run and tool-call id and fingerprinted over exact tool name and arguments. A receipt never becomes claimable merely because 24 hours elapsed: this native-only scope uses the maximum safe integer expiry sentinel, while HTTP scopes retain their existing TTL. Quick-chat deletion removes these receipts by owned run id; account purge removes every owner's idempotency row. Replays check fresh run authority and cannot override a later owner move. A first-time collection no-op records its receipt without reordering and witnesses the tree version. | Build default after adversarial review | §3.2, §6.1, §8.1, §8.7; SI18, SI20 |

## Phase E — populated visual evidence

| ID | Decision | Basis | References |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EV.1 | **Theme comparison frames use real persisted content and Violet.** Each theme/mode/viewport receives the same five API-created tasks and Git-backed page. Desktop selects the portfolio task; laptop and mobile keep the populated collection visible as the primary surface. Mobile retains the existing 3× device scale factor. This 36-frame matrix verifies populated workspace composition, not all-screen or populated-chat acceptance. | Build default | §10.3, §17; workspace_now and themes briefs |
| EV.2 | **Interactive control boundaries cannot borrow decorative divider contrast.** Task completion checkbox borders use contrast-adjusted muted ink. The notification control on the top bar uses chrome-specific ink, hover and focus tokens. Browser regressions require at least 3:1 for unchecked checkbox boundaries and notification icons; the original Tide Light controls failed at 1.86:1 and 1.80:1 respectively. | Visual audit defect repair | §10.3; note 02; WCAG non-text contrast |

## Connections UI defaults

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D2UI.1 | **Connection resources are memory-only and reopen after effect cleanup.** Live catalogue discovery runs only while browsing or on the optional onboarding step, never into browser storage. Account refresh hints coalesce into one in-flight read and at most one follow-up. StrictMode effect replay reopens the resource and mutation lifecycle; old results are fenced by an epoch. The only handoff storage is validated task navigation ids, scoped by owner and access generation, so the fixed provider callback can return to the initiating task without storing a URL, catalogue or credential. | Build default | §7, §14.2–14.3; connections and onboarding_connections |
| D2UI.2 | **Incoming-agent setup defaults to selected tasks and read access.** All current/future tasks require a deliberate selection; subtasks are selected individually. Task choices use explicit cursor pages, not an unbounded preload. API keys are masked, revealed/copied only on demand, held only in component memory, and removed on close or account/access change. Unknown mutation outcomes freeze the exact input and idempotency key; a redacted replay offers explicit revoke-and-replace. OAuth consent and the fixed-origin post-login bridge stay in the analytics-excluded consent route group. | Build default | §6.1, §14.4–14.5; R11; agent_connections |
| D2UI.3 | **The onboarding gate preserves only the provider callback outcome enum.** The API still redirects exclusively to Settings → Connections. If that exact path meets an account still on the optional connections step, the app gate carries only connected, failed or cancelled to the onboarding route. It never propagates an arbitrary next path, provider URL, nonce or other query parameter. | Adversarial integration fix | §14.2; onboarding_connections |
| D2M4 | **Simon Sharing tools reuse the claimed document session and return private references only.** Snapshot/proposal/handoff use the existing encrypted Sharing services; release and raw capability URLs remain owner-UI-only. Quick chat exposes only bounded artifact/grant listing. Revocation folds an exact run/tool-call receipt in `simon.native.sharing`, with current authority in its deciding batch and the retained-run expiry convention from D2M3. Worker grant events are owner-checked hints, never authority; handoff analytics uses the same fresh-consent service with immediate bounded worker delivery. No ARTIFACT_ORIGIN is added to worker configuration. | Build default; executor parity and race review | §6.1, §8.1, §13, §15; D2M3 |

## Phase E — live findings

| ID | Decision | Basis | References |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EL.1 | **Missing D1 rate-limit headers preserve the conservative shared budget.** Cloudflare's current public API documentation says successful REST responses carry `Ratelimit` and `Ratelimit-Policy`, but the live D1 `/query` endpoint returned neither for both configured tokens on 2026-09-20. The live contract treats a complete pair as measurable and a complete absence as an explicit `unknown`; a partial pair still fails. No rate assumption is relaxed: the API/worker split remains 2 + 1 requests per second until a future live run can measure scope. | Live D1 contract; provider discrepancy | §3.1–3.2; C3-2 |
## Simon Connections/Vault integration

| ID | Decision | Basis | References |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D2E.13 | **A Vault handle is a review-time placeholder, never an alternate provider value.** The wrapper overlays the exact single-key `{\"$vault\": grantId}` shape onto live input schemas for proposal/edit validation, then validates resolved plaintext against the unchanged live schema. Session and metadata work finishes before resolution; after decryption only in-memory validation and the final run/connection authority fence precede the no-retry provider call. Both executors use this seam. Quick chat rejects every handle, and every returned value crosses the mandatory Vault redactor before a result, checkpoint, model or output sink. | The provider schema ordinarily rejects an object where its eventual value is a string; resolving during proposal or API edit validation would violate the Vault and durable-API boundaries. | §8.3–8.5, §11.3, §14.1; R2, R5, R12 |

## Simon handoff screen integration

| ID | Decision | Basis | References |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D2M5 | **Handoff-screen drafting is an ordinary task-conversation turn with a reference-only client request.** The owner-initiated request contains the reviewed revision, selected private artifact ids, destination enum and typed outcome, but no document/artifact plaintext. Simon reads bounded sections through its existing tools and returns the terminal encrypted-history reply to the editable UI. Generation creates no artifact, proposal, grant, link or external send; saving and release stay separate trusted-UI actions. The resumable idempotency intent survives surface timeout/unmount, while each mounted caller owns only its abortable wait. | The original callback had neither selected references nor lifecycle cancellation, and its synchronous-looking `Promise<string>` did not account for durable runs. Extending it with `artifactIds` and `AbortSignal` preserves the seam while using identical local/Trigger execution. | §8.1–8.3, §8.7, §13.1; handoff brief; note 16 |

## Phase E scripted browser contracts

| ID | Decision | Basis | References |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D2M6 | **The explicit test/development model may recognize a narrow encoded document-edit directive.** The directive drives one bounded section read, one revision-guarded section replacement and a terminal reply through the production Simon loop and tools, so the browser can prove chat-to-page realtime integration without a paid provider or fabricated HTTP response. Its fields are schema-shaped, it is never logged, ordinary scripted prompts keep the inert response, and production continues to reject scripted mode at model resolution. | Phase E needed an executable browser proof for the document-tool flow; the existing fixed scripted response could prove chat transport but could never call a tool. | §8.1, §8.3, §9.4, §17; Phase E flow 5 |
| D2M7 | **Production Next builds use webpack while development retains Turbopack.** Next 16.3.5 on Node 24 reproducibly stopped making progress at `Creating an optimized production build ...` while emitting the full and selectively narrowed async route graphs; clean caches and prebuilt package outputs did not change it. The supported webpack compiler completes the same clean build in seconds. `next.config.ts` mirrors the exact four browser-safe source aliases as absolute webpack aliases, and a regression test proves both maps resolve to the same package source exports, so the clean-clone/no-`dist` invariant remains intact. Revisit Turbopack production only after the upstream deadlock is fixed. | Phase E release-gate defect; consistent with upstream vercel/next.js#97398. | §2.2; F1, F5 |
| D2M8 | **A private share password form may accept the browser privacy value `Origin: null` only with an independent same-origin Fetch Metadata witness.** The viewer's `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` causes a navigation-mode form POST to serialize its origin as literal `null`. `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` is therefore required for either an absent or `null` Origin; `same-site`, `cross-site`, missing Fetch Metadata and every foreign concrete Origin remain forbidden. The per-render form nonce is still mandatory. | Browser integration defect and CSRF review | §5.3, §13.3; D2D.3 |

## Phase G — deployment defaults

| ID | Decision | Basis | References |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | **The public API and isolated artifact surface share one paid Render Docker service, selected by hostname.** Production uses the current smallest paid compute id `0.5c-512mb` in Singapore, waits for Git checks, probes `/healthz`, gives WebSockets and in-flight requests 60 seconds to drain, and repeats the idempotent D1 migrator before traffic moves. `api.symplist.tejassuds.com` and `artifacts.symplist.tejassuds.com` terminate on the same service; the artifact hostname remains distinct so application cookies never reach it. | Phase G brief; current Render Blueprint and compute-plan documentation; §13 host isolation | §2.2, §3.4, §5.3, §13, §16 |
| G2 | **The first Render deployment starts with one trusted proxy hop and must verify it before admitting users.** Render terminates TLS at its public load balancer and forwards HTTP to the container. `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=1` makes Express and the WebSocket limiter agree on the client address. The publish smoke must compare a controlled request's address in both paths; any additional owner-configured proxy requires increasing the count before production traffic. | Render edge topology; the architecture required a measured first-deploy value but supplied no default | §3.1, §5.8, §16.2 |
| G3 | **Vercel owns only `apps/web`, but installs and builds from the workspace root.** The Vercel project root is `apps/web`; its checked-in config moves each command to the repository root for the Corepack-pinned pnpm 12.4.2 install and filtered Next build, leaving `.next` as the framework output. Production public variables stay in the Vercel environment rather than Git. | Vercel monorepo and Corepack guidance; shared browser-safe workspace packages | §1, §2.2, §4.5, §16.2 |
| G4 | **Simon uses provider prompt-prefix caching, never application response memoization.** OpenAI GPT-5.6 requests opt into implicit 30-minute caching without a caller cache key; a live contract requires an actual cache read. Every run is still freshly authorized and bounded to ten steps, 4,096 requested output tokens per step, 8,192 total, a 40-message/64-KiB history suffix, and 96 KiB of provider-controlled connector output. Cache read/write counts are content-free run telemetry. The message route has a 12/minute pre-D1 client-network bucket, while beta plan quotas remain disabled as note 07 requires; operators must also configure a dedicated provider project with a hard spend limit. | Launch cost/privacy audit; live OpenAI cache contract; free-beta product rule | §3.1, §5.8, §8.1, §8.3, §8.5–8.6; note 07 |
| G5 | **The Simon submission bucket is scoped to an authenticated session inside its client network.** The before-D1 limiter hashes the session cookie and never retains the bearer token; missing sessions fall back to the network key. Independent signed-in users behind one NAT therefore do not consume one another's 12/minute model-start budget, while every request is still shed before database/model work. This is burst containment, not the disabled beta-plan quota. | The full three-viewport suite exposed that a network-only key made unrelated authenticated sessions sharing loopback/NAT exhaust one another's budget. | §3.1, §5.8, §8.1; G4 |
